Explore legislation and public policy across the Middle East and North Africa. What this observatory is

A trilingual research catalogue of legislation, public policy and source evidence. It separates what a source says from what has been verified, records open interpretation questions, and does not issue legal advice or compliance certificates.

Rules as Code, made visible

Rules as Code turns written rules into structured logic that a machine can apply. This example is synthetic: Axiom RuleSpec declares inputs and derived judgments in YAML, while Legalese L4 expresses CONSIDER/WHEN steps, MAYBE values and a deontic MUST duty.

Axiom RuleSpec — machine-readable excerpt

Declarative inputs and derived judgments. The full source compiles to an Axiom artifact; this page does not execute it.

- name: procurement_obligation
    kind: derived
    entity: Procurement
    dtype: Judgment
    sources:
      - citation: "Synthetic procurement policy s.1 (fictional)"
        url: https://example.org/synthetic-procurement-policy
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2026-01-01'
        formula: facts_complete and covered_body and contract_scope_met and not exception_applies
  - name: open_source_consideration_required
    kind: derived
    entity: Procurement

Axiom RuleSpec source

Legalese L4 — machine-readable excerpt

A ladder of CONSIDER and WHEN steps with MAYBE and deontic expressions. The synthetic page renders a readable ladder and dependency graph.

`procurement outcome` covered_body contract_scope_met exception_applies contract_value MEANS
    CONSIDER covered_body
    WHEN NOTHING THEN Indeterminate
    WHEN JUST FALSE THEN NotApplicable
    WHEN JUST TRUE THEN
        CONSIDER contract_scope_met
        WHEN NOTHING THEN Indeterminate
        WHEN JUST FALSE THEN OutsideScope
        WHEN JUST TRUE THEN
            CONSIDER exception_applies
            WHEN NOTHING THEN Indeterminate
            WHEN JUST TRUE THEN ExceptionApplies
            WHEN JUST FALSE THEN
                IF contract_value >= 100000
                THEN OpenSourceConsiderationRequired
                ELSE RequirementWithoutOpenSource

DECLARE Party IS ONE OF ContractingAuthority

Legalese L4 source

Short excerpts from the committed synthetic sources. No real legislation is encoded.

Legalese-style ladder (excerpt)

  1. Step 1 Are the required facts complete?

    If true: Continue to coverage · If false: Indeterminate

    SP-3

  2. Step 2 Is the public body covered?

    If true: Continue to scope · If false: Not applicable

    SP-1

  3. Step 3 Is the contract within scope?

    If true: Continue to exceptions · If false: Outside scope

    SP-1

How evidence is reviewed

The stages are distinct. A record may stop at any stage; this page does not imply that every record has completed the full pipeline.

  1. Source discovery Find an official instrument or policy page and record the lead.
  2. Evidence capture Record what was retrieved, when, and whether bytes or only metadata were held.
  3. Provision identification Record exact locators and short excerpts where permitted; do not invent missing structure.
  4. Interpretation Record candidate meanings, alternatives and questions without treating them as settled.
  5. Review Qualified human review is recorded separately; the build cannot supply it.
  6. Optional rule encoding Only reviewed interpretations may feed an executable rule; no real reviewed encoding is published.

Source discovery and evidence capture can establish that a page was found and retrieved. They do not establish legal meaning.

Research coverage and limitations

The observatory records research activity, not compliance. Jurisdictions, policy areas and records differ in evidence state, and absence of a record is not evidence that no law or policy exists.

Evidence states include reported sources, retrieved official pages, captured metadata, document excerpts, full documents where available, and unreviewed interpretation questions. A successful retrieval does not establish legal authenticity, currency, commencement or binding effect.

An empty cell, a missing record, or an open question means the research has not established an answer. It does not mean that no law exists, that a duty does not apply, or that a country has no policy. This site records that difference explicitly instead of turning uncertainty into a “no”.

What this release does not claim

  • No compliance certification for any organisation or website.
  • No country ranking or comparison score.
  • No draft policy treated as law in force.
  • No link presented as proof of legal effect.
  • No machine-executable rule described as legally approved.
  • No claim that every listed jurisdiction or policy area has been researched.
